newsitem.title: UK: UK Liberal Democrats call for HK probe.
newsitem.headline: UK Liberal Democrats call for HK probe.

text.p: Britain's Liberal Democrats on Monday called for a probe into the negotiations that led to the handover of Hong Kong to China.

In a rapidly escalating row over the role of Hong Kong's last governor Chris Patten, the centrist party asked: "Was the Conservative government selling the people of Hong Kong down the democratic river?"
"If secret deals were being made with China to ensure that the introduction of democracy was delayed, then the public must be told," it said.
The Foreign Office is conducting an investigation into allegations that Patten leaked secret documents to writer-broadcaster Jonathan Dimbleby.

Officials said police were not involved in the ministry probe. The decision on whether Patten should be interviewed will be taken by the inquiry team. He is currently writing a book at his holiday home in France.
Former Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said he did not think ministry officials were out to get Patten.
Britain's new Labour government on Sunday confirmed press reports that authorities are investigating the allegations.
"That will be done in a proper, objective and authoritative way," minister without portfolio Peter Mandelson said.
His comments came after The Sunday Times said Foreign Office officials were pressing for Patten to be prosecuted under Britain's Official Secrets Act.
But Rifkind, the Conservative foreign secretary until May, doubted any targeting.

"The Foreign Office, like the civil service as a whole, are absolutely loyal to the government of the day and I don't believe they would allow any personal views of that kind to colour the way in which they carried out their responsibilities," he told BBC radio.

"For two years I handled Hong Kong policy as foreign secretary and I regularly discussed these issues with my advisers ... Some of them may have had their personal views but I got nothing but absolutely loyal support for the policy which was the policy of the government," he added.

Patten is alleged to have leaked to Dimbleby details of a secret British deal with China in the 1980s over the future of Hong Kong, which was handed back to China at the end of June after 156 years of colonial rule.
The Sunday Times said the row was sparked by its publication of extracts from Dimbleby's recently published book on Governor Patten's time in office.

Patten was said to have been angry at Britain's failure to bring in direct elections in Hong Kong from 1988 in order to hand over a democratic administration in China. He is said to have claimed London gave in to China.
